summary: Tina Rasmussen specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Pa-Auk Sayadaw and under MA supervisor Christian K. Wedemeyer.

Tissa Rajapatirana is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University (1966–1974) under Jan Willem de Jong and held a post there in the Department of South Asian and Buddhist Studies (attested 1988).
Tiziana Pontillo works in the fields of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.
Todd A. Gibson is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under György Kara and earned his PhD at Indiana University (attested 1991).

Todd Thornton Lewis works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under numerous mentors and held posts at the College of the Holy Cross, where he was attested as professor from 1996 to 2017.

Tokan Tada was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Sera Monastery (1913–1923). He later taught at Tohoku University (circa 1931–1945) and held a post at the University of Tokyo (circa 1945–1953).
Tokio Takata is a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University (circa 1968–1976) and later held a post there from circa 1988 to 2014.
Tokugen Sakai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Tokuno Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara. He held teaching posts at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Fukui Chugakko, and Toyo University.

Tokuryu Yamauchi was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University (circa 1916–1919). He later held posts at Kyoto University of Education, Kyoto Institute of Technology, and Ryukoku University.

Tom J. F. Tillemans is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held a post at the University of Lausanne (attested 1987–2018), where he is Emeritus Professor, and served as Visiting Numata Chair at the University of Calgary.

Tomoko Masuzawa works in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale University, and UC Santa Barbara (~1979–1985), and held faculty posts at UNC Chapel Hill (~1987–2000) and the University of Michigan (1999, ~2000).
Tomoyasu Oshima specializes in Indology and linguistics. Attested in 2012, Oshima studied under Toshifumi Goto and held a part-time lecturer post at Kyoto University.
Tomoyuki Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University and held a post there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Tomoyuki Uno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 1998), the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 1998), and as an assistant professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).

Tomy Augustine works in philosophy and Indology. He earned a master's at the University of Madras studying under C. S. Sundaram, completed a PhD at Banaras Hindu University under Munni K. Agrawal, and held a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

Toni Huber specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison and William Sax, and held professorships at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 2000) and Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 2006–2008).

Tony K. Stewart is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976). He held posts at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011).

Torkel Brekke specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned an MPhil at the University of Oslo and a doctorate at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich, later holding posts at Oxford (~1995–1999) and Oslo (~2001–2021).

Toru Haneda was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1903–1907) and held a post at Kyoto University from circa 1907 to 1945.
